newsitem.title: PANAMA: U.S., Panama to hold talks on anti-drug center.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Panama to hold talks on anti-drug center.

text.p: U.S. and Panamanian officials will meet on Monday for continued "routine talks" on turning strategic Howard Air Force Base in Panama into an international anti-drug centre, a government spokeswoman said on Sunday.
Veteran diplomat John Negroponte, the U.S. coordinator for the Panama bases negotiations, will meet with Jorge Ritter, head of Panama's transition team, a Foreign Ministry spokeswoman said.
"The assistant foreign minister said Negroponte will meet with Ritter tomorrow for a routine meeting on the anti-drug centre," she said, although she was uncertain where the talks would be held.
Previous informal talks between Negroponte and Ritter have been held in Miami, she said.
Negroponte chairs the Interagency Working Group on Panama, which is reviewing a possible post-1999 U.S. presence in Panama.

The United States and Panama are discussing a proposal to turn strategic Howard Air Force Base, located at the Pacific Coast entrance to the Panama Canal, into an international centre for anti-drug efforts.

Panamanian President Ernesto Perez Balladares had said Panama would not enter into talks with the United States to negotiate a military presence in Panama in the next century. But he said the United States could keep Howard in Panama at no cost for use as an anti-drug centre.
The United States is to turn over control of the Panama Canal and withdraw all troops and bases by Dec. 31, 1999, in accordance with bilateral canal treaties.
